summary: Sand Point Lighthouse, on the Saint John River in Kings County, New Brunswick: a light since 1869 and a 1898 wooden tower, a heritage lighthouse of 2016 still owned by the Canadian Coast Guard.

access.note: Grounds open; tower closed. The wharf beside the lighthouse is private.

events.note: Six beacon lights, including Sand Point, put into service on the Saint John River on 20 August 1869.
J. Cauldfield, first keeper at Sand Point.
Open-framed mast replaced by a new enclosed tower, completed 1898 by G. W. Palmer of Kars for $699.
Entire superstructure above the iron framework painted white on the opening of navigation in 1901.
Recognized by the Government of Canada as a heritage lighthouse.

notes_for_editor: Keeper dates for Sand Point come from LighthouseFriends' list, the only source found for most names. The Department's keeper lists in the corpus (1914 and 1915 volumes) were not matched to Sand Point because OCR columns are split, so nothing there confirms the 1913-1923 names. Wagner is confirmed in the 1906 and 1907 statements of lightkeepers by page image (scan pages 342 and 180; printed pages 261 and 171; appointed 1883 at $80 a year), so the story now cites printed pages. The 1901 painting is in the printed report on p. 64 (scan p. 79), confirmed by the corpus. Current light characteristic conflicts: LighthouseFriends' table says 'Continuous red light' (so the JSON uses that, which is consistent with the record's F R); its 1898 description says the light is fixed white. The record gives focal height 22.8 m, which differs from LighthouseFriends' 22.7 m; the JSON uses 22.7 m. The story gives no current characteristic. The register text is cited through Heritage Guide's reproduction of Canadian Register of Historic Places entry no. 20933 (recognized 14 June 2016). The Parks Canada page itself was not usable with fetch_text (it drops the page body, which sits inside a form element), and the Directory id 15154 given in earlier notes was not confirmed; the quotes are verified against the Heritage Guide copy. The record's 'first_lit 1869' comes from Rowlett, and LighthouseFriends agrees. The Canadian Coast Guard owns it per LighthouseFriends; the register text does not give an owner. A 1910 corpus entry ('Sand point, Erection of a 22-foot wooden lighthouse tower') is not used: it may be a different Sand Point (Nova Scotia or Chats Lake, Ontario). Private residents at the cottages are not named. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts are paraphrased and only short quotes are used.
